title: FTM engine - customer-facing API contract for FTM-WEB.COM
source_of_truth: docs/contract.json in the engine repository, generated by hand from the route files; the CHANGELOG below lists every deploy that changed something for the website.

statuses_legend.live: deployed and answering on the public hostname
statuses_legend.coming: in the engine code and proven, answers after the next API restart (until then the old process answers 404 NOT_FOUND)

customer.description: Every /customer/... route and GET /billing/status. The website backend verifies the Supabase session server-side and asserts who the customer is. The engine never sees a customer password or a browser JWT. A brand-new customer works at once: the first authenticated call creates the customer record. Besides each route's own errors, every customer route can answer 401 UNAUTHENTICATED, 403 CUSTOMER_NOT_PERMITTED, 409 EMAIL_ALREADY_REGISTERED and 503 CUSTOMER_API_NOT_CONFIGURED.

headers.Authorization: Bearer <FTM_WEBSITE_API_TOKEN>  (the website's server-side token; never in a browser)
headers.X-FTM-Auth-Email: <the customer's email>  (used only on first sight to fill the customer record)

website_token.description: System-to-system calls with the same Bearer token and no customer subject (PUT /billing/subscription).

none.description: No header at all (health, this contract page).

conventions: Every response is JSON with ok: true | false. An error is { ok: false, error: "CODE", ...details }; the CODE is one of the errors listed below, each with a text the site may show as is.

Every { ok: false, error } answer carries message: plain words for the customer (from error-texts.js, or a more specific sentence the route wrote). Show message when you have no translation for the code. Live from the next API restart; until then message is present only where the route wrote one.
Request bodies are validated strictly: an unknown field is a 422 VALIDATION_FAILED with issues: [{ path, message }], never silently dropped.
Money fields are strings (numeric from the database, e.g. "7635.54000000"), never floats; null means not reported yet. Render an absence, never a zero.
Dates are ISO-8601 UTC strings. account_id is a public uuid; internal ids never leave the engine.
account_number is a string of digits (MT5 logins can carry leading zeros).
The same 404 ACCOUNT_NOT_FOUND answers an unknown id, a malformed id, somebody else's account and a removed account; the three are deliberately indistinguishable.
Three connected accounts per customer, one of them trading (is_trading). The others read status_reason PAUSED, shown as 'Connected - not trading'.

An FTM master login added by a customer becomes a view-only row (view_only: true, status PAUSED, label 'View only - FTM master account'): statistics, history, performance and remove work; activate, pause and password change answer 409 MASTER_ACCOUNT.

Master preview (8 Nov 2026): every customer without a view-only master row of their own, free customers included, gets one extra card in GET /customer/accounts: account_id f7a00000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001, view_only: true, preview: true, preview_note, account_number and server null. It is not one of their accounts and never counts toward account_limit. GET history, positions, performance and stats answer for it; every control route (pause, resume, activate, risk_tier, password, remove, close a position, stats refresh) answers 404 ACCOUNT_NOT_FOUND.

display_status.PAUSED: Connected - not trading. (status_reason PAUSED, PAUSED_DRAWDOWN; every view-only row.)
display_status.INACTIVE: Connected, trading switched off by FTM or no strategy enabled.
display_status.OFFLINE: No terminal or no heartbeat right now. status_reason NO_NODE_ASSIGNED = 'Verified, being set up by FTM'.
display_status.SETUP_INCOMPLETE: Login details submitted, not yet verified by FTM (NEVER_VALIDATED) or being verified again after a password change (VALIDATION_PENDING).
display_status.ACTION_REQUIRED: The broker refused the login details or the account cannot be used as submitted; see validation_reason (NOT_CONNECTED, NOT_HEDGING, LOGIN_MISMATCH, WRONG_SERVER -- the account is on another server name of the broker: broker_server_hint names it; remove the account and add it again with that server) and can_retry_password.
display_status.SETUP_FAILED: FTM could not set the account up (SETUP_FAILED, BELOW_MINIMUM, CANNOT_TRADE): show the 'contact support' text.
display_status.MAINTENANCE: The platform is in maintenance; nothing is copied until it ends.

routes.summary: Liveness of the engine.
The signed-in customer: public id (put it into Stripe's client_reference_id), subscription, how many accounts.

200.client_id: FTM-1A2B-3C4D5E (FTM- + the first 10 hex characters of customer_public_id, upper case; stable and unique forever)

routes.summary: Subscription status of the signed-in customer. copies_allowed is what the planner checks before every copy while billing is switched on.
The website's Stripe webhook handler forwards each event. Idempotent per stripe_event_id; EXEMPT (set by FTM) is never overridden.

request.note: one of customer_public_id, email, stripe_customer_id is required

routes.summary: Connect an MT5 account. 202 (not 201): accepted, verified by FTM within minutes; the card then moves through the statuses. A master login becomes a view-only row.

body.password: <the MT5 master password, never the investor password>

request.note: strict: no other field. Choosing GROWTH is recorded automatically; the connect form carries no acknowledgement field.

routes.summary: Every connected account of the customer (removed ones are gone). Key the texts on display_status / status_reason; everything else is information. Every row also carries deposits / withdrawals (balance operations read by the statistics sync, so Gain % never counts a deposit as profit), last_synced_at (the sync) and last_reported_at (the terminal heartbeat, else the sync, else the master records). For an account without a copy terminal the balance / equity / floating fields hold what the sync read. (deposits / withdrawals / last_synced_at: from the next API restart.) 9 Nov 2026 LONG-POLL for the connect screen: ?wait_for=<account_id>&since=<that account's status_signature>&wait=<0-25 s> holds the request until that account's status changes (or the wait ends) and then answers exactly as without it; header X-FTM-Wait: changed | timeout. Every GET also sends an ETag: send If-None-Match to get 304 when nothing changed.

accounts.status_signature: <32 hex: changes whenever the status can change; send it back as ?since= with ?wait_for= to long-poll>

routes.summary: Pause trading: no new copies; open copies stay and close with the master. Body { close_open: true } = pause and close everything now.

200.note: No new trades are copied; open trades still close with the master.

routes.summary: Trade on this account (resume / switch): it becomes the customer's one trading account; the account that was trading closes its open copies and becomes 'Connected - not trading'. /resume is the same route.

200.note: This account copies from the next master trade. The previous account closes its open copies and its terminal is released.

routes.summary: Alias of /activate.
Change the risk profile. New copies use the new tier from the next master trade; open copies are untouched. GROWTH needs growth_acknowledged: true (the sentence comes back in the 409).

Closed trades, newest first, with a summary, in ONE shape for every connected account (trades[], page.total). 10 Nov 2026: EVERY account, the trading one included, answers its own STATEMENT (source ACCOUNT_HISTORY: every closed position, FTM's copies and the customer's own trades, from the read-only statistics sync; re-read about a minute after each copy closes) -- the same rows as GET /stats history_page; each row has copied_by_ftm (true = FTM copied it; ftm_test / welcome_trade / label / closed_by from the copy record). symbol = the master's name where the broker's symbol is mapped (market = the broker's symbol); ?symbol= matches either. Before the first read: the trading account its copy records (source FTM_COPY, copied_by_ftm true), a view-only row the master records. Query ?limit=50 (1-200) &offset=0 &symbol=XAUUSD. net_profit = realized + commission + swap (null when a component is unknown). (One shape for every account: from the next API restart.)

200.source: ACCOUNT_HISTORY | FTM_COPY (trading account not read yet) | FTM master records (view-only row not read yet)

routes.summary: Open positions, in ONE shape for every connected account (positions[]). The trading account: open copies. An account without a copy terminal: its own open positions from the statistics sync's latest snapshot (plus balance, equity, currency, snapshot_at); a view-only row falls back to the master's heartbeat positions. (One shape for every account: from the next API restart.)

FTM's copies on this account: the daily balance / equity curve since connect, monthly % returns, max drawdown, the drawdown brake's figure, totals per market. A view-only row answers the master's figures.
Close one open copied position now. The terminal executes it within seconds; it then appears in the history.

202.note: The close is executed by your terminal within seconds; it then appears in your history.

routes.summary: New MT5 master password after the broker refused the old one (offer it only while can_retry_password is true). Three tries in total; FTM re-verifies and, if a terminal runs, rebuilds it (deprovisioning: true).

Remove the account. Works for every account (hand-built terminals and view-only rows included). The card is gone at once; FTM takes the terminal down in the background. Refused only while copied trades are open.

The account's own statistics (balance, equity, P/L, deal history with deposits and withdrawals, growth, drawdown) read from the account itself by ONE general read-only sync, for every account the customer added: trading, paused, connected-not-trading and the view-only master row. data_source: STATS_SYNC after the first read; LIVE_TERMINAL while the trading account's terminal reports fresher numbers; MASTER_RECORDS for a view-only row before its first read; FTM_COPIES for an account never read. Before the first read of an ordinary account: pending: true with a message; poll every 15-30 s while refreshing is true. Full field list: docs/client-area-stats-api.md (served as /api/v1/dev/contract.json#docs).

query.offset: 10 Nov 2026: history rows to skip (whole number >= 0); kept for paging, but use before_deal
query.before_deal: 10 Nov 2026: STABLE page cursor -- the ticket of the last row of the previous page (history_paging.next_before_deal); a deal that closes between two requests never shifts the pages
query.as_of: 10 Nov 2026: ISO time -- only rows at or before it (send back history_paging.as_of of page 1 to freeze the view)
query.risk_days: keep only the last N days of risk_score_history (1-36500)

split.rule: per position (net of all its deals); ftm.closed_pl + own.closed_pl = closed_pl_total; fees_and_adjustments in neither; pl_pct time-weighted over that side only

200.risk_score_basis: 30-day equity volatility (50 %), current drawdown from the equity peak (30 %), margin use now (20 %); deposits and withdrawals excluded

200 (pending).message: FTM is reading this account now; statistics appear within about two minutes.

routes.summary: Ask FTM to read the account again now (a second, read-only login, within one to two minutes), for any account the customer added, the trading one and a view-only row included. Idempotent while one is queued. 409 ACCOUNT_NOT_CONNECTED only for an account that is neither connected nor view-only.

202.note: FTM reads this account read-only within about two minutes; ask for the statistics again after that.

routes.note: The ACCOUNT_NOT_CONNECTED text: an account that is neither connected nor view-only cannot be logged into.

routes.summary: The FTM master's statistics in the same shape as /stats (from the master's own data). Query ?limit=, ?master_id=. The missing array lists what the master does not report yet; show it as a footnote.
The customer's support conversation (created on first call): status, unread (badge it, poll every 30 s), support_online, attachment limits.

Messages, oldest first. Query ?after=<message_id>&limit=50 (1-200) for new ones (poll every 3-5 s with after=cursor while the chat is open; an empty list is normal), ?before=<message_id> for history. Deleted messages come back with deleted: true and an empty body.
Send a message. 201 with the message; the same client_message_id again answers 200 with the same message (repeated: true). A message reopens a CLOSED conversation.

Upload a file: a RAW body (not JSON) with headers Content-Type: <an allowed type> and X-FTM-File-Name: <original name>. Put the attachment_id into a message within an hour, otherwise the file expires.
The file bytes (Content-Disposition: attachment), only for the conversation's owner and only once attached to a message.
Read receipt: { up_to: <message_id> } or {} = everything. Call it when the chat is visible.

A single-use 60-second ticket for the browser's EventSource on /api/v1/chat/stream?ticket=… (events: ready, message, read, presence, ping). That path needs one Cloudflare Access bypass rule before a browser can reach it; until then poll GET /customer/chat/messages.
The same SSE stream with the normal customer headers, for a backend that can hold the connection (not a short-lived serverless function).
The browser SSE path: ?ticket=<from POST /customer/chat/ticket>; the ticket is the only credential. The engine closes a stream after 30 minutes; EventSource reconnects with a fresh ticket.

The whole investment picture for the client area: the terms (payments_enabled false = deposits are confirmed by FTM by hand), the FTM account's unit index, and the customer's contract (the open one, else the latest ended one; null for a customer who never invested). Money strings in EUR; the index tracks the FTM account's percentage return, no currency conversion. Valuation: gross_value = units x index; gross_profit = gross_value - capital; customer_share = 50% of a profit, a loss in full; customer_value = capital + customer_share. Terms 2026-11-06 with carry-over: on first_withdrawal_on (the 1st of the month after 13 full months) and on each anniversary before the end (about months 13, 25, 37, 49) an allowance of 20% of the profit share not yet withdrawn on that day unlocks; every unlocked allowance not yet taken stays available until the end and can be withdrawn at any time, in one or several requests (one waiting at a time); withdrawable_now = unlocked_total - profit_withdrawn - pending, never above the profit share now; the capital is never withdrawn and stays locked until ends_on (5 years), when the capital and the remaining profit share are paid out.

terms.first_withdrawal_rule: 1st of the month after 13 full months
terms.withdrawal_rule_text: from the 1st of the month after 13 full months, and again every 12 months until the end, 20.00% of your profit share not yet withdrawn becomes available; what you do not take stays available and can be withdrawn at any time later, in one or several requests
terms.capital_locked_rule: your capital stays invested until the end of the 5-year term; then the capital and the remaining profit share are paid out

contract.refund_available_on: 2031-11-20 | null (= ends_on: the capital is locked for the whole term)

allowances.amount: 200.00 (20% of the profit share not yet withdrawn that day)

withdrawals.withdrawable_now: 350.00 (unlocked_total - profit_withdrawn - pending, never above profit_share_now; 0.00 before first_withdrawal_on and from ends_on)
withdrawals.next_unlock_on: 2030-01-01 | null (the next allowance; null after the last one)
withdrawals.window_start: 2029-01-01 | null (older name: the last unlock day)

routes.summary: REQ-003 / REQ-010: the investment page's rows, one per contract of the customer (newest first, ended ones included), with the monthly history (closed statements + the running month marked live). Rows come from contracts the customer started in the client area (POST /customer/investment/contracts) and FTM confirmed by hand; payments stay OFF, so nothing is created from a Stripe payment yet.

investments.joined_at: 2026-11-06 (the day the first deposit was confirmed; the request day while PENDING_FUNDING)
investments.refund_from: 2031-11-06 | null (= ends_on: capital locked for the whole term)
investments.value_now: 1800.00 (what the customer would be paid now)
investments.profit_to_date: 300.00 (the customer's share; negative = the loss, which is not split)
investments.withdrawable_now: 350.00 (the unlocked yearly allowances not yet taken; "0.00" while locked)
investments.next_withdrawal_on: 2026-11-06 | 2028-01-01 | null (today when something can be withdrawn now, else the next unlock day)

routes.summary: REQ-003: the Withdraw button. Without a body it requests everything withdrawable right now (withdrawable_now: the unlocked yearly allowances not yet taken); with { amount } that amount; several requests are fine, one waiting at a time. 202 requested:true; a repeat of the same client_request_id answers 200 repeated:true. Refused with the INVESTMENT_* codes (each with message): INVESTMENT_LOCKED carries allowed_from and locked_until (the first unlock day), INVESTMENT_WITHDRAWAL_LIMIT withdrawable_now and next_unlock_on (with nothing left its message names that day), INVESTMENT_EXCEEDS_VALUE customer_value, INVESTMENT_CONTRACT_NOT_OPEN from the end day (everything is paid out together).

Start a contract with the first deposit INTENT (minimum 1,000.00; terms_version must equal terms.terms_version; client_request_id is the idempotency key: a repeat answers 200 repeated:true with the same body). Nothing is paid through the engine: the website shows FTM's payment instructions and FTM confirms the arrival by hand; the contract becomes ACTIVE on that day.

deposit.kind: DEPOSIT | WITHDRAWAL | REFUND | PROFIT_SHARE_FTM | CONTRACT_END | ADJUSTMENT

routes.summary: A further deposit intent into the running contract (minimum 100.00; 1,000.00 while the contract is still PENDING_FUNDING).

deposit.kind: DEPOSIT | WITHDRAWAL | REFUND | PROFIT_SHARE_FTM | CONTRACT_END | ADJUSTMENT

routes.summary: Request a withdrawal (terms 2026-11-06, carry-over): at most withdrawable_now = the yearly 20% allowances unlocked so far (first_withdrawal_on and each anniversary) minus profit withdrawn and pending; any time, in one or several requests, one waiting at a time, never capital. Paid by FTM by hand out of the profit only: the capital stays; amount / 50% of gross profit leaves the contract (the customer gets the amount, FTM realizes its equal half). From ends_on: refused, the term is paid out together.

withdrawal.kind: DEPOSIT | WITHDRAWAL | REFUND | PROFIT_SHARE_FTM | CONTRACT_END | ADJUSTMENT

routes.summary: Ask for the payout at the end of the term (terms 2026-11-06: the capital is locked until refund_available_on = ends_on, 5 years after the start; earlier -> INVESTMENT_LOCKED with allowed_from): the contract becomes REFUND_REQUESTED and FTM pays the capital plus the remaining profit share at that moment; a loss is the customer's. estimated_value is the value when asked.

refund.note: paid at its value when processed; a loss is yours

routes.summary: Cancel a PENDING deposit intent, withdrawal or refund request of the caller. Cancelling a refund puts the contract back to ACTIVE; cancelling the only deposit of a PENDING_FUNDING contract cancels the contract (a new one may be started).
Every ledger row of the contract, newest first (limit 1..500, default 100; before=<entry_id> pages back). PROFIT_SHARE_FTM rows show FTM's realized share; ADJUSTMENT rows carry FTM's note.

entries.kind: DEPOSIT | WITHDRAWAL | REFUND | PROFIT_SHARE_FTM | CONTRACT_END | ADJUSTMENT

routes.summary: Closed monthly statements, newest first (a month is closed by the engine on the first pass of the next month).

statements.closed: true for a stored month, false for the running month (computed live)
statements.profit_withdrawn_to_date: 0.00 (profit share paid out to the customer up to the closing day)
statements.withdrawable_close: 0.00 (what could be withdrawn on the closing day; null on months closed before 2026-11-06)

routes.summary: One month (YYYY-MM): the stored row for a closed month, the live figures (closed:false) for the running month.

statement.closed: true for a stored month, false for the running month (computed live)

website_to_engine.description: The website team asks the engine for changes by editing ONE file in their own repository. The engine polls it every 30 minutes (no token: the repository must stay public-readable, or the team gives FTM a read token), stores every entry and mails FTM about every new open item within about 35 minutes. Answers come back in the CHANGELOG below, by id.

format.entry_heading: ## REQ-<number> (open|done) <YYYY-MM-DD>   followed by a bold one-line title on the next line: **Title**
format.body: free Markdown under the title until the next '## ' heading: what the site needs, the route or field, an example request/response if you have one, who asked.
rules: One entry per request; ids are REQ-001, REQ-002, ... and are never reused. (WR-001 [open] title, with the status in brackets and the title on the heading, is accepted too.)
status is 'open' until the engine's CHANGELOG answers the id; then the website team flips it to 'done' (or 'dropped'). A missing status means open.
Newest first is fine; order does not matter to the engine. Anything before the first '## REQ-' heading is ignored (use it for an intro).
A new open entry is mailed to FTM once. Editing an entry's text or status is recorded, not mailed. Re-opening a done entry mails it once more.
A 404 for the file means 'nothing yet' and is not an error.
format.example:
# Website requests to FTM ENGINE

Newest first. FTM ENGINE answers by id in its changelog.

## REQ-002 (open) 2026-11-06
**Show the broker's server time on the account card**
The card shows last_reported_at in UTC; we would like the broker's server offset too.
Route: GET /customer/accounts, new field server_utc_offset_minutes.

## REQ-001 (done) 2026-11-05
**Error text for MASTER_ACCOUNT**
Answered in the engine changelog 2026-11-05.
